metaDescription: Leaf blower vacuum mulchers compared on mulch ratio, impeller design, corded versus cordless power and bag size, with picks for small and mid-size yards.
expertTake: The MZK 40V brushless is the best cordless 3-in-1 here for its 700 CFM claim and anti-jam tube, the Heywork corded 40L unit is the value pick, and the WORX Trivac is the proven small-yard choice. Skip these for big lawns of wet oak leaves: a bagging mower or a tow-behind vacuum does that job better.
introParagraphs: A 3-in-1 leaf tool is a blower with a second life. Swap the nozzle for an intake tube and bag, and the same fan pulls leaves in, chops them with an impeller and packs the shreds into a bag. Shredding is the real prize, because a bag of chopped leaves holds many times what a bag of whole leaves does.

The tradeoffs are mechanical. The impeller that does the chopping is also what jams on wet leaves and twigs, the motor type sets runtime or cord reach, and the bag size decides how often you stop. This guide compares those factors across corded and cordless models so you can pick the one that survives a full fall season.

products.name: MZK 40V Brushless 3-in-1 700 CFM 40L Bag
products.description:
MZK pairs a brushless motor with a claimed 700 CFM and 180 MPH and a 40-liter bag. Brushless means less heat and wear, which matters in a tool whose fan and impeller load swings sharply when leaves enter the intake. A 10-second turbo mode gives short bursts for stubborn spots.

The anti-jam design is the feature that earns the top spot. An internal suction tube keeps the joints from catching leaves and the square connector resists twisting, addressing the most common complaint about 3-in-1 tools. Switching between blow, vacuum and mulch is tool-free.

The tradeoff is battery. Turbo draws hard, and vacuum mode drains faster than blowing, so keep a spare pack for a big yard. Empty the bag before it packs tight, because a full bag chokes airflow and wastes energy. Feed leaves in steadily and avoid stuffing the tube, since a clean feed rate keeps the impeller from bogging.
products.bestFor: Mid-size yards where cordless freedom and anti-jam design matter.
cons: Vacuum mode drains the battery fast
Platform is newer with less support
Turbo is limited to short bursts

products.name: Heywork 40V Cordless Brushless 600 CFM
products.description:
Heywork's cordless unit is a slightly smaller sibling of the MZK on paper: 600 CFM and 160 MPH from a brushless motor, with four speed settings and a turbo boost. Multi-speed control matters because vacuuming and mulching want full power while sweeping a patio does not.

It costs less than the MZK and gives up some airflow and the anti-jam tube design. For dry leaves on a small or mid-size yard it is a capable machine.

Manage the battery as you would any cordless tool: keep it indoors, charge before use and carry a spare for long jobs. Use the lower speeds for sweeping and save turbo for vacuuming. Keep the intake screen clear so the motor does not run hot.
products.bestFor: Cordless buyers with small to mid-size yards who watch cost.
pros: Lower price tier than the MZK
cons: Less airflow than the MZK claim
Battery limits runtime in vacuum mode

products.name: Heywork Corded 3-in-1 450 CFM 40L Bag
products.description:
A corded motor never runs down, so this Heywork can vacuum and mulch for as long as the cord reaches. It claims 450 CFM, 158 MPH and a 15:1 mulch ratio, meaning fifteen bags of whole leaves shrink to roughly one. The 40-liter bag is large for the class.

The cord is the cost. You need a heavy-gauge outdoor extension cord, and the work area is limited to its reach, so large yards become an exercise in cable management. Against the cordless units it also lacks airflow.

For a small yard near an outlet it is the cheapest dependable option. Keep the intake clear of twigs and unplug before clearing any jam. Feed it dry leaves in handfuls rather than one big rake pile, which keeps the shredding even.
products.bestFor: Small yards and driveways near an outdoor outlet.
cons: Cord limits reach and can tangle

products.name: CRAFTSMAN 3-in-1 12 Amp Corded 450 CFM
products.description:
CRAFTSMAN delivers the highest air speed in this guide, up to 260 MPH, with 450 CFM from a 12-amp corded motor. High air speed lifts wet, matted leaves off hard surfaces, which is where low-speed tools fail.

Tool-free conversion between blower, vacuum and mulcher is a convenience, and the backpack-style bag carries the weight on your shoulders instead of one hand. A 12-amp circuit limits real power, so the numbers are maker maximums.

The cord remains the limit. Compared with the cordless MZK, it has a faster blast but less freedom. It is a good all-around corded choice if you value speed. Wear safety glasses, since high air speed throws grit and the mulcher flings fragments.
products.bestFor: Driveways and patios with matted leaves near an outlet.
pros: 260 MPH peels wet leaves off hard surfaces
cons: 450 CFM is modest for big piles

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 3-in-1 Backpack 400 CFM PowerBoost
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER's design puts the bag on your back with up to twice the capacity of its earlier bags, and a zipper-free wide opening makes emptying quick. A PowerBoost button raises output on demand to 250 MPH and 400 CFM.

Carrying the bag on your back is genuinely less tiring than a shoulder bag over 20 minutes, though a full backpack bag adds noticeable weight. The corded motor means unlimited run, bounded by the cord.

Compared with the CRAFTSMAN it offers a similar speed and a more convenient bag at a slightly lower airflow. Empty it before it packs too full. Adjust the harness before each session, because a poorly fitted backpack bag pulls on your shoulders.
products.bestFor: Mid-size yards where bag convenience matters more than cord freedom.
cons: Backpack bag is heavy when full

products.name: WORX Trivac WG509 12 Amp 350 CFM 18:1
products.description:
WORX's Trivac has been a staple of the category for years: a 12-amp corded motor, up to 350 CFM and 210 MPH and an 18:1 mulch ratio, the highest in this guide. A higher ratio means each bag holds more shredded leaves.

The airflow is lower than the newer cordless units, so large piles take longer. Its strengths are a compact body, a long track record and an easy tool-free conversion for patios, driveways and turf.

Store it with the cord coiled and check the impeller for wear after seasons of twigs. Treat it as the compact option for patios and tight spaces. Check the impeller for wear after a season of twigs and acorns.
products.bestFor: Small yards where mulch ratio and a proven design matter.
pros: 18:1 mulch ratio is the highest here

products.name: PULITUO Corded 3-in-1 530 CFM 170 MPH

specList.label: Function
specList.value: Blower, vacuum and mulcher with bag

products.description:
PULITUO claims 530 CFM and 170 MPH with a 15:1 mulch ratio from a corded motor, the highest airflow among the corded models here, though the figure is a maker maximum. The listing says fifteen bags of leaves reduce to one.

It is a value unit for owners who want volume more than speed. Against the Heywork corded unit it claims more airflow for a similar price tier.

Keep the intake clear and use a heavy extension cord. Check the return policy and parts availability before buying, since the brand is newer. Keep the vents clear so the motor sheds heat.
products.bestFor: Corded buyers who want more airflow at a low price tier.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Mulch ratio and what it means
buyingCriteria.explanation: A ratio like 18:1 on the WORX Trivac or 15:1 on the Heywork corded unit says how many bags of whole leaves shrink to one of shreds. Higher ratios mean fewer trips to the curb or compost. Ratios are claims and fall with wet leaves. A fair test is to ask how often you will empty the bag: a better ratio means fewer trips.

The impeller chops leaves, and wet leaves, twigs and acorns are what jam it. The MZK's internal suction tube and square connector are built to resist clogging. Plastic impellers wear faster than metal ones, so ask which you are getting. Pull the tube apart after each session and check the joints, since leaf paste builds up where parts meet.

Corded units such as the CRAFTSMAN and Heywork corded never run down but are bounded by the cord. Cordless units like the MZK and Heywork 40V give freedom but drain faster in vacuum mode than in blow mode. If you already own a 40V battery family, a bare cordless tool is the cheaper route.

Air volume moves piles and air speed peels wet leaves off pavement. CRAFTSMAN's 260 MPH suits matted leaves, while MZK's 700 CFM suits piles. Figures are maker maximums. Remember that peak speed and peak volume rarely occur together on the same tool.

A 40-liter bag, as on the MZK and Heywork units, cuts stops. A backpack bag as on the BLACK+DECKER spreads weight but is heavy when full. A packed bag also chokes airflow. Fill a bag with a bucket of leaves at home to see how full it feels in your hand.

Never put hands near the impeller. Unplug or remove the battery before clearing a jam, and wear eye and ear protection, since mulching throws debris and the impeller is loud. Hearing protection is worth wearing too, because shredding is louder than plain blowing.

specDecoder.meaning: How many volumes of whole leaves are reduced to one of shreds. It is a best-case claim. It drops when leaves are damp or the bag is nearly full.
Cubic feet per minute of air at the nozzle. More volume moves more leaves per pass. Treat it as a ranking tool, not a promise.
Air speed at the nozzle. It lifts wet, matted leaves.
Motor current. A 12-amp motor draws near the limit of a 15-amp household circuit. A thin cord will overheat or sag under load.
A motor without carbon brushes, cooler and more efficient. It stretches battery runtime. It also makes the tool lighter than a brushed equivalent of similar output.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mulching hardware
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared mulch ratios from 15:1 to 18:1 and impeller design, giving credit to the MZK's anti-jam tube. Mulch ratios are best-case numbers, so we gave only modest weight to the highest claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed CFM and MPH as maker maximums, noting MZK at 700 CFM and CRAFTSMAN at 260 MPH. We noted that CFM and MPH are not comparable across brands, so they were used to rank only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: We balanced cord reach on the corded units against battery drain in vacuum mode on the cordless ones. Cord reach was treated as a real limit, since extension cords add resistance and trip hazards.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bag and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at bag size and carry style, including the 40-liter bags and the backpack design. Bag fit and emptying ease were compared, since they decide how often you stop.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated the Heywork corded as the value pick from the MZK as the overall pick. Owner feedback patterns on jamming shaped the scoring. Owner feedback patterns on jam frequency carried more weight than any single spec.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The CRAFTSMAN, WORX, Heywork corded, PULITUO and BLACK+DECKER never run down, but you manage a cord.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The MZK and Heywork 40V move freely, but vacuum mode drains batteries fast.

howToChoose.note: Pick corded for small yards near power, cordless for freedom on larger ones.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for high air speed and an anti-jam design. Wet leaves clump and stick in the tube.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The CRAFTSMAN at 260 MPH peels leaves off pavement and the MZK's anti-jam tube resists clogging.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your yard is larger than a quarter acre, which points to the MZK 40V.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if the yard is small. The Heywork corded or WORX Trivac handles it for less.

maintenance.why: Wet leaf residue and twigs build up. Unplug or remove the battery first.
Chipped or worn impellers cut poorly and vibrate.

maintenance.task: Empty and shake out the bag

maintenance.why: A nicked cord is a shock hazard.
Keep lithium packs at partial charge.

faq.q: Do vacuum mulchers handle wet leaves?
faq.a: Poorly. Wet leaves clump and jam the tube. Work in dry conditions or in small amounts.

faq.q: What does a 15:1 mulch ratio mean?
faq.a: Fifteen bags of whole leaves reduce to roughly one bag of shreds. It is a best-case claim.
Corded never runs down but needs a heavy cord. Cordless frees you but vacuum mode drains batteries quickly.
Small twigs only. Larger ones jam or damage the impeller.

faq.q: Are mulched leaves good for the lawn?
faq.a: Shredded leaves break down fast and feed the soil. Thick layers still smother grass.

faq.q: Is it safe for pets and children?
faq.a: Keep them clear. The impeller is a hazard and debris is thrown.
